standard_prerequisites.name: The characterization of universally closed morphisms by the existence part of the valuative criterion, cited from the schemes chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces universal closedness of the given morphism to the existence of the dotted arrow in a valuation ring diagram.

standard_prerequisites.name: Reductions of schemes and the behaviour of morphisms and dense images under passage to the reduction, together with the description of the scheme theoretic image in the reduced case, cited from the schemes chapter and the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the proof assume all schemes reduced and rewrite density of the image as the scheme theoretic image being the whole space.

standard_prerequisites.name: Flatness of a polynomial algebra over the coordinate ring of an affine open and invariance of the scheme theoretic image under flat base change, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the scheme theoretic image of the base changed dense open is the whole of the polynomial algebra's spectrum.

standard_prerequisites.name: Existence of a valuation ring diagram reaching a prescribed point of a scheme theoretic image, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the valuation ring A' and the field K' whose closed point maps to the point of interest.

standard_prerequisites.name: Existence of a valuation ring inside a residue field dominating the image of a given valuation ring, and the description of a valuation ring sandwiched between a valuation ring and a residue field, both cited from the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Builds the valuation ring A'' and the auxiliary valuation ring C that put the situation into the shape of the hypothesis.

core_obligations: Set up the criterion: to prove the morphism universally closed it suffices to solve a solid diagram built from a valuation ring A with fraction field K, which is the shape appearing in the hypothesis (proof lines 10236-10243).

Reduce the situation: since valuation rings and fields are reduced one may replace the three schemes by their reductions, density of the image becomes the statement that the scheme theoretic image of the dense open is the whole space, and the base may be taken affine (proof lines 10244-10252).

Base change to a flat polynomial algebra: choose an affine open of the source through which the field valued point factors, take a polynomial algebra surjecting onto the fraction field, and use flatness and invariance of scheme theoretic images under flat base change to see that the base changed dense open has image the whole polynomial spectrum (proof lines 10254-10259).

Produce the auxiliary valuation rings: apply the existence statement for valuation diagrams reaching points of the scheme theoretic image to obtain a valuation ring A' with fraction field K' whose closed point maps to the chosen point; then choose a valuation ring inside the residue field dominating the image of A and form the sandwiched valuation ring C, which together with its fraction field fits into a diagram of the shape required by the hypothesis (proof lines 10260-10288).

Extract the dotted arrow: the hypothesis supplies a dotted arrow for the diagram built from C and K', uniqueness forces its composite with the natural map from the larger valuation ring to agree with the given morphism, and restricting to the residue field of A' produces an element x of the source whose local ring maps into the dominating valuation ring; maximality of A in the domination order inside K then forces the image of that local ring to lie in A, which yields the arrow from the spectrum of A (proof lines 10289-10302).

Separatedness: when the morphism is quasi-separated its diagonal is quasi-compact, and a solid diagram for the diagonal is the same data as a pair of morphisms out of the spectrum of the valuation ring; uniqueness forces that pair to factor through the diagonal, so the already proved result applies to the diagonal and the dense open, showing the diagonal universally closed and hence the morphism separated (proof lines 10304-10327).
proof_roadmap: Reduce universal closedness to the valuative criterion and simplify the situation to reduced schemes with an affine base (proof lines 10236-10252).

Replace the source by a flat polynomial algebra cover, build the auxiliary valuation rings whose residue fields drive the hypothesis, and pull the dotted arrow back to the original valuation ring using maximality for domination (proof lines 10254-10302).
Apply the same result to the diagonal to obtain separatedness under the quasi-separated hypothesis (proof lines 10304-10327).
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a refined valuative criterion: if a quasi-compact morphism has a quasi-compact dense subscheme through which every valuation ring diagram admits a unique filler, then the morphism is universally closed, and separated as well when it is quasi-separated (statement lines 10219-10234). The counted proof is long and technically dense: it reduces to reduced schemes and an affine base, passes to a flat polynomial algebra cover so that the base changed dense open has the whole spectrum as scheme theoretic image, applies the existence statement for valuation diagrams to produce an auxiliary valuation ring, then invokes the existence of a dominating valuation ring inside a residue field and a sandwich construction to put the situation into the shape required by the hypothesis, and finally pulls the dotted arrow back to the original valuation ring by maximality for the domination order (proof lines 10236-10302); the separatedness half is deduced by running the same argument for the quasi-compact diagonal (proof lines 10304-10327). It is H2: the argument is a complete author proof with several genuinely distinct reduction steps, and the cited inputs are standard criteria and algebra facts.
